text: {"en": ["I have seen the account of the aforementioned elders, the sharpness of their answers to the questions put to them, and the honor they received from the king on their account. It reminded me of a similar account of an actual event which, not being well-worn, may please the listening ear.", "Therefore \"my thoughts prompt me\" [Job 20:2] to set it down in this book, all the more since it is the way of our Rabbis to bring together all matters of this kind that resemble one another, \"two on account of one,\" so that a single remembrance of them may rise in our minds.", "First, however, I shall copy here how they too, of blessed memory, related it in the chapter Lo Hayu Koftin; this is their wording there:", "It was taught: Alexander of Macedon asked the elders of the Negev ten things.", "He said to them: \"Is the distance from the heavens to the earth greater, or from east to west?\" They said to him: \"From east to west.", "You may know this, for when the sun is in the east everyone can look at it (a), and when the sun is in the west everyone can look at it;", "when the sun is in the middle of the sky no one (b) can look at it.\"", "But the Sages say: \"The two are equal, as it is said: 'For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is His steadfast love' etc. [Ps 103:11],", "'As far as the east is from the west' etc. [Ps 103:12]. And if one of them were greater, Scripture should have written (c) both with the one that is greater.\" Then what is the reason that when the sun is in the middle of the sky no one can look at it?", "Because it stands exposed and nothing covers it (d). He said to them: \"Were the heavens created first, or the earth?\" They said to him: \"The heavens were created first, as it is said: 'In the beginning God created the heavens' [Gen 1:1].\"", "He said to them: \"Was light created first, or darkness?\" They said to him: \"This matter has no solution.\"", "But let them tell him that darkness was created first, as it is written: \"And the earth was formless and void, and darkness\" [Gen 1:2],", "and afterwards, \"And God said, Let there be light\" [Gen 1:3]! They thought: perhaps he will go on to ask what is above (e), what is below (f), what is before (g), what is after (h).", "If so, they should not have told him about the heavens either! At first they thought it was merely a chance question;", "once they saw that he kept on asking, they said: \"Let us not tell him, lest he go on to ask.\"", "He said to them: \"Who is called wise?\" They said to him: \"One who foresees what is to come.\"", "He said to them: \"Who is called mighty?\" They said to him: \"One who conquers his inclination.\"", "He said to them: \"Who is called rich?\" They said to him: \"One who rejoices in his portion.\"", "He said to them: \"What should a man do to live?\" They said to him: \"Let him put himself to death (i).\"", "\"What should a man do to die?\" \"Let him keep himself alive.\" He said to them: \"What should a man do to be accepted by people?\" They said to him: \"Let him hate kingship and dominion.\"", "He said to them: \"Mine is better than yours: let him love kingship and dominion and do good to people.\"", "He said to them: \"Is it better to dwell at sea or on dry land?\" They said to him: \"On dry land,", "for all seafarers have no peace of mind until they come up onto dry land.\"", "He said to them: \"Which of you is the wisest?\" They said to him: \"We are all equal alike,", "for every matter you have put to us we have solved for you together.\"", "He said to them: \"Why have you opposed (j) us?\" They said to him: \"Satan prevailed (k).\"", "He said to them: \"I shall have you killed by royal decree.\" They said to him: \"Power is in the king's hand, but falsehood does not befit a king (l).\"", "At once he clothed them in purple and placed a chain of gold upon their necks [b. Tamid 31b–32a].", "Thus far. Now from this wording of our Sages of blessed memory it is evident that these elders were Israelites.", "However, the writer Plutarch, in the Life of Alexander of Macedon, section 137,", "and likewise Clement of Alexandria, whom we mentioned above, in the sixth book of his Stromata, related this story and wrote that it took place with the sages of India,", "who had incited their king Sabbas to rebel against Alexander; and they told it in a manner different from the one cited above.", "For this reason I have translated it from the Latin and set it before you.", "Alexander of Macedon captured ten sages who had been inciting the king of Sabbas to rebel against him,", "and who were adept at answering profound questions briefly.", "He put perplexing questions to them and warned them that the first who did not answer properly would surely be put to death, and the others likewise in order,", "and he appointed the eldest of them all as judge over them. Then he asked the first, saying:", "\"Whom do you consider more numerous, the living or the dead?\" He answered: \"The living,", "for the dead no longer exist at all.\" He asked the second: \"Which breeds larger living creatures, the sea or the land?\" He answered: \"The land, for the sea is part of it.\"", "He asked the third: \"Which is the most cunning of living creatures?\" He answered: \"The one that man has not yet come to know.\"", "He asked the fourth: \"For what reason did you incite the king of Sabbas to rebel against me?\" He answered: \"So that he would choose to live free rather than die a slave.\"", "He asked the fifth: \"Which do you think came first, the day or the night?\" He answered: \"The day, by one day.\"", "And seeing the king apparently scoffing, he said to him: \"To one who asks subtleties, such answers are fitting.\"", "Then the king changed his approach and asked the sixth: \"How can the ruler of a great kingdom win the hearts of all?\"", "He answered: \"By being good to all and not instilling fear.\" Of one of the three remaining he asked: \"How can a man be numbered among the gods?\" He answered: \"By performing deeds that exceed human power.\"", "Of another he asked: \"Which do you consider stronger, life or death?\" He answered: \"Life,", "for it endures so many afflictions and hardships.\" And of the ninth, who was the last, he asked:", "\"Until when is it good for a man to live?\" He answered: \"Until death seems preferable to him over life.\"", "The king then turned to the one he had appointed judge and said to him: \"Judge them.\"", "He answered: \"Each one answered worse than the other.\"", "He said to him: \"In that case you shall die first.\" He answered: \"My lord king, if you keep the utterance of your lips, that would not be fitting,", "for you said you would put to death first the one who did not answer properly.\"", "Alexander then bestowed much honor and gifts on them all and sent them away in peace.", "Explanation: he saved the earlier ones by saying that each prior one was found to have answered correctly relative to the one after him,", "and he saved himself, for the king had said he would put to death the first, and he had no second after him.", "However, the Ḥartumei Miẓrayim, in the book of the Life of Alexander that I have, translated into Hebrew, ⚠", "and likewise Curtius, an ancient Roman writer, in his work about Alexander, wrote nothing at all of these questions;", "nor did Arrian the Greek, whom I consider more reliable on him than any writer, and who wrote in the preface to his work that the core of his account derives from the narratives of King Ptolemy son of Lagus, Alexander's general during his wars,", "and from the narratives of Aristobulus of the Aristobuli, a Jew according to the Latin Lexicon, ⚠", "though he is not the one who wrote on the Torah of Moses, mentioned in the previous chapter;", "for this Aristobulus the writer was one of Alexander's commanders.", "And in his eighth book this Arrian mentioned the gymnosophists, that is, the sages of India,", "but not these questions. Likewise the Josippon of the Romans is silent about them.", "True, in [the Josippon] of the Hebrews, book 2, chapter 11, there is mention of them under the name of the sages of India, but that account (whoever its author was) does not resemble any of the versions we have mentioned; ⚠", "and since it is a work found among our people as it is, I did not trouble to copy here what is written there.", "It is also possible that the words of our Sages and the words of the aforementioned Plutarch are both true, [referring to] two events: the one with the sages of Israel and the other with the sages of India."], "notes": [{"seg": 6, "note": "The bracketed letters (a), (b), etc. here and below reproduce the Vilna edition's marginal note markers (א), ב), etc.); the markers in seg. 26 (יח)) and 27 (יב)) are reproduced as printed."}, {"seg": 30, "he": "סימן קל\"ז", "note": "The section number reflects the edition de' Rossi used; the episode is ch. 64 in modern editions of Plutarch's Alexander. Kept as given."}, {"seg": 31, "he": "בספר הששי מן הסטרומא\"טי", "note": "Reference kept as given by the author; not verified against modern editions of Clement's Stromata."}, {"seg": 56, "he": "חרטומי מצרים מצרים", "note": "The phrase (with doubled מצרים) is unclear; it seems to designate the Egyptian magicians/sources of a Hebrew Alexander romance (cf. the Nectanebo tradition). Transliterated rather than identified."}, {"seg": 59, "he": "הערוך הרומיי", "note": "Literally 'the Roman Arukh', apparently a Latin lexicon (perhaps Calepino); identification uncertain. 'Of the Aristobuli' (מן האריסטו\"בולי) is also obscure."}, {"seg": 64, "he": "(למי שהיה)", "note": "The parenthetical, literally 'for whoever was', is taken as a doubt about the authorship of the Hebrew Josippon; the sense is uncertain."}]}
